# AAT JWS Test Vectors (draft-niyikiza-oauth-attenuating-agent-tokens-02)

Generated by `gen_vectors.py`; do not edit by hand. every expected verdict below was reproduced by the self-checking §8 verifier in that file. These vectors follow the -02 text. Tokens use `alg` `Ed25519` (RFC 9864) rather than -01's `EdDSA`, so an unmodified -01 verifier rejects nearly every vector; Appendix F of the draft lists the other verdict changes.

## Vector ids

A vector's id is `J.<group>[.<n>]`, where the group is its topic (below). `cbor_twin`, where set, names the vector `A.x` in Tenuo's CBOR suite (`docs/spec/test-vectors.md`) that encodes the same scenario, with the same key seeds and timestamps. 29 of the 229 vectors have a twin; otherwise group numbers have no relation to the CBOR suite's section numbers.

## Conventions

- Signature algorithm: Ed25519, JWS `alg` = `Ed25519` (RFC 9864).
- AAT headers carry `typ` = `aat+jwt` and PoP headers carry `typ` = `aat-pop+jwt` (RFC 8725 §3.11, as DPoP uses `dpop+jwt`). Verifiers reject a missing or mismatched `typ` at the header step (3a, 4a, 7a). Draft-01 defines no `typ`.
- `aat_aud` is OPTIONAL in the PoP; when present it MUST identify the receiving enforcement point (step 7d). AATs MAY carry `aud`, checked for every token in the chain (step 6c). PoP JWTs MAY carry an enforcement-point `nonce` (step 7h). Each vector states which of these its enforcement point requires under **Policy**. Draft-01 leaves audience to deployment policy without defining the value.
- In `all` subsumption, every parent clause must subsume at least one derived clause; a derived clause MAY cover several parent clauses; extra derived clauses are permitted. Draft-01's one-to-one assignment is dropped (it adds backtracking without adding soundness).
- AAT and PoP payloads are JCS-canonical (RFC 8785) except where a vector deliberately carries other bytes: an inadmissible number, number syntax that JCS would rewrite, a duplicate member, or a non-canonical layout (J.27.2). Each token records `payload_jcs_canonical`; a verifier MUST verify the presented bytes and MUST NOT re-canonicalize before checking a signature.
- `par_hash` = base64url-nopad(SHA-256(parent JWS Signing Input)), where the signing input is the ASCII string `BASE64URL(header) || '.' || BASE64URL(payload)` (§4.6). J.12.b shows the wrong (payload-only) form.
- Derived `iss` = `urn:ietf:params:oauth:jwk-thumbprint:sha-256:<RFC 7638 thumbprint of the signing key>`.
- `jti` values follow the CBOR vector IDs: `tnu_wrt_019471f8...0001` becomes `019471f8-0000-7000-8000-000000000001`.
- No non-ASCII strings or escaped characters appear anywhere. Numbers with a fraction or exponent appear only where a vector tests them: in invocation arguments (J.8.12-J.8.14) and in claims whose syntax §3.2 restricts (J.20.14, J.21.13, J.21.16, J.21.17, J.24.4-J.24.6). Number admissibility (§3.4) is covered by J.8.7-J.8.14. A harness must read `args_json` and each `payload_json` with a parser that keeps a number's exact value and whether it was written with a fraction or exponent; a parser that converts to doubles cannot detect either.
- The expected verdict follows the -02 text. The expected step is the first failing step in §8's order; an implementation that orders independent steps differently can report another step for the same vector, so harnesses compare verdicts.

| Trust anchors | `control_plane` public key, bound to issuer `https://auth.example.com`; `control_plane2` public key, bound to issuer `https://auth.example.org` |

## Coverage of Section 8

Each DENY vector differs from a valid presentation by one fault. `gen_vectors.py --mutation-check` disables each check of the generator's verifier in turn (the lettered steps, the §3.4 well-formedness rules, each `check` predicate and §4.5 subsumption rule, and the empty-map and entry-type normalizations) and requires at least one vector to change verdict. The checks below cannot be the only fault in a presentation, because another check always fails with them; no vector depends on them alone. 4f and 5 are among them.

| Check | Why it is never the only fault |
|---|---|
| `1:empty` | an empty chain has no root, so no later step can reach PERMIT |
| `2c:extract` | a jti that is not a string also fails 3j (root) or 4b1 (derived) |
| `3k:uri` | the trust anchor's issuer is a URI, so a root iss that is not one also fails 3k:anchor |
| `3l:jwk` | without a cnf.jwk the next signature check (4b or 7b) fails |
| `3m:array` | without the array there is no attenuating_agent_token entry, which fails 3m:one |
| `3m:tools` | an entry without a tools object authorizes no tool, so 6b fails |
| `4b2:jwk` | without a cnf.jwk the next signature check (4b or 7b) fails |
| `4b3:array` | a token without the array has no attenuating_agent_token entry, which fails 4n:one |
| `4b5:strings` | a missing or non-string iss fails 4c, and a missing or non-string par_hash fails 4q |
| `4e:parent-max` | child.del_depth > parent.del_max_depth means 4g or 4m fails as well |
| `4f:max` | del_depth <= del_max_depth <= the root's del_max_depth <= MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH (4m, 4g, 3i) |
| `4n:tools` | an entry without a tools object authorizes no tool, so 4p1 or 6b fails below it |
| `5:length` | 3c and 4d already make len(chain) equal leaf.del_depth + 1 |
| `6a:one` | 3m and 4n already require exactly one entry in every token, the leaf included |
| `6b:star` | the * constraint is always a wildcard (3n, 4o), which accepts every value |
| `7c:strings` | aat_id and aat_hash are compared with the leaf (7c) and aat_tool with the tool (7e) |
| `7c:hta` | the invocation's args are an object, so a missing or non-object hta fails 7f |
| `wf:object` | a constraint that is not an object cannot be evaluated by any later step |

## J.9.6 A tool named only by a scope claim in a derived token

L1 of the J.3 chain carries a scope claim (RFC 8693 Section 4.2), "read_file search_index delete_file", which names delete_file; neither L1's attenuating_agent_token entry nor the root grants it. The invocation is delete_file. Only the leaf's attenuating_agent_token entry authorizes a tool (step 6b), and claims this specification does not define carry no authority in a derived token (Section 3.3); a verifier that read scope as a grant would accept.

The invocation passes id = 9007199254740992 (2^53), which is admissible. The PoP's hta writes id as 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1), which rounds to the same double and so has the same JCS form; the canonical forms match, but the signed number is not admissible (Section 3.4), so step 7f denies.

> Read the invocation from args_json with a parser that keeps every number's exact value; a parser that rounds to doubles cannot tell admissible from inadmissible numbers.
